blueprint_conformance_check.confidence: MEDIUM - single rater, primary-category-only coding, no official per-question classification is published.
blueprint_conformance_check.dimension_of_care_tolerance_detail: All four dimensions fall inside the published tolerance under this coding: health promotion 16.4% (15-25), acute 32.7% (30-40), chronic 32.7% (25-35), psychosocial 18.2% (10-20).
blueprint_conformance_check.finding: The free set behaves like a blueprint-sampled miniature of the exam: all four physician activities AND all four dimensions of care fall inside the published tolerance bands under single-primary-category coding. That makes it a defensible structural reference for item style, and it means a study bank aiming at MCCQE realism should sample the same eight categories in the same proportions.
blueprint_conformance_check.method: One primary physician activity and one primary dimension of care assigned per question by a single rater, then compared with the published MCC blueprint tolerances.

copyright_and_use.source_document: MCCQE practice questions and answers (2026 edition PDF)
statements: The 55 official questions are published by the MCC for personal study and non-commercial use.
No stem text, option text, rationale text or reference list from the official set is reproduced in this artifact.
No derivative paraphrase of any individual official question is stored.
Every rationale_for_classification field describes item structure only and is written so that the underlying clinical scenario cannot be reconstructed from it.
Counts, distributions and structural labels are original analysis, not MCC content.

lead_in_form.most_common_lead_in: Which one of the following is the best next step?
lead_in_form.second_most_common: Which one of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

deterministic_structure.note_on_option_count: Directly contradicts any assumption of a fixed five-option MCCQE item. The 2010 MCC MCQ guideline describes five options as the construction default; the current published practice set uses 3, 4 or 5. Generation should therefore treat 4 or 5 as acceptable and must not manufacture a fifth option to hit a quota.

rationale_format.implication_for_this_project: The official rationale format is exactly the per-distractor defeat statement the pipeline already produces. It is external confirmation that a distractor-by-distractor discriminator is expected, not optional.

reference_format.implication_for_this_project: Official practice items cite current external clinical authority per item. This matches the repository's evidence-claim contract and argues against treating any single textbook as the authority.
observed_source_families: guideline or society statement (including Canadian: CMPA, Canadian Task Force)

difficulty_claim_boundary.classification_provenance: EASY/MEDIUM/HARD values in this artifact were assigned by this research from item structure alone, by a single rater, using the rubric in the companion design document. They are a MODEL STRUCTURAL DIFFICULTY ESTIMATE and must always be reported with that label.
difficulty_claim_boundary.legitimate_use: Internal rubric calibration against professionally written items, and the observation that officially published items are not uniformly hard.
difficulty_claim_boundary.what_it_does_not_support: Any published MCC Easy/Medium/Hard band, percentage, or per-item difficulty label. An ordered booklet establishes that a range exists; it does not describe the shape of that range.
difficulty_claim_boundary.what_official_evidence_supports: MCC operational items span a range of empirically measured difficulties. The MCC estimates item difficulty empirically (p-value), performs classical item analysis and Rasch calibration, treats roughly 0.20-0.90 as the usable p-value range, and standard-set the 2025 exam with the Bookmark method, which requires an item booklet ordered from easiest to hardest.

difficulty_correlates_observed.EASY_profile: One salient decisive feature stated almost in the words of the key; two or three competitors, at least one separable on category or on sight; recognition or one-step application.
difficulty_correlates_observed.HARD_profile: Three or more features integrated, or a sequencing or threshold judgement; every competitor stays live because each is anchored on a real datum in the stem; the decisive move is often that the most salient datum does NOT meet its own threshold, or that a remote history item reframes the presentation.
difficulty_correlates_observed.MEDIUM_profile: Two or three features must be integrated or a rule applied to given data; three live competitors in one response class; one decisive discriminator that a prepared candidate finds reliably.
difficulty_correlates_observed.label: MODEL_STRUCTURAL_DIFFICULTY_ESTIMATE
difficulty_correlates_observed.note: In the hard items the competitors are defeated by positively stated data requiring inference, not by written-in denials. This is the same LIVE_BUT_INFERIOR signature the repository's stem-anchor work already isolated, observed independently in official material.

distractor_findings.finding: Not one of the 55 requires a trick, a withheld fact or specialist-board trivia. Difficulty is produced by how many stem features must be integrated and by how close the live competitors are, never by obscurity. Harder items in the set carry MORE live competitors, not fewer and weaker ones.

mcc_distractor_standard_alignment.note: LIVE_BUT_INFERIOR is this repository's own term. No claim is made that the MCC uses it. Official MCC item-writing guidance establishes the properties the term names.
official_properties_supporting_it: distractors must be consistent with the stem
options must form a homogeneous response class
distractors should be drawn from common misconceptions and real candidate errors
distractors must be incorrect or definitely inferior to a defensibly best key

model_structural_difficulty_estimate_dis.caveat: MODEL_STRUCTURAL_DIFFICULTY_ESTIMATE. Assigned by this research from item structure alone, by one rater. The MCC does not publish Easy/Medium/Hard labels for these 55 questions, and the published set carries no candidate-level statistics, so no empirical p-value, discrimination or option-endorsement value can be derived from it. 21.8 / 54.5 / 23.6 is NOT MCC empirical difficulty, NOT an MCC official difficulty classification, and NOT a real-exam difficulty distribution. It is also not evidence that any study-bank mix matches the MCC.
model_structural_difficulty_estimate_dis.label: MODEL_STRUCTURAL_DIFFICULTY_ESTIMATE

questions.rationale_for_classification: Every option restates the same statistic under a different misreading, so all four competitors are canonical misconception distractors on one response class. One definitional discriminator decides it.
Two history features must first be integrated into a syndrome class, then mapped to a confirmatory test. All options are investigations of the same organ system, so the response class is homogeneous.

One explicitly reported laboratory value redirects the standard pathway; the pathway-default option is the strongest competitor and is what an unanchored candidate selects. The decisive datum is printed but easily skipped.
The stem states the defining features of the keyed entity almost verbatim. One option is a disease entity among syndrome labels, a mild homogeneity break that further separates the set.

Requires recognising an unnamed syndrome from two dispersed features and then selecting the associated comorbidity to probe. The lead-in asks for a history item rather than a diagnosis, adding an inferential step.
All options are disclosure actions on one axis running from full release to outright refusal. One consent principle decides it; the partially-correct refusal option is the main competitor.
Numeric options compete with one principle-level option, a partial parallelism break. The decisive step is applying a stratified rule rather than recalling a single number.
All options are agents in the same therapeutic class family. The discriminator is a single mechanism-linked adverse-effect property; near-class competitors stay live.
Options are all members of one nosological category and the stem supplies several prototypical criteria of the key. Recognition-level.
Duration, preserved function, absent hallucinations and retained affect must be integrated jointly; no single feature decides. One option sits outside the response class and is separable.
A canonical communication principle with one clearly best action; two options are defensive or dismissive and separate on sight.

The stem plants two competing causal cues plus one examination finding that excludes the most-endorsed option. Competitors remain strongly live and the resolution requires weighing cues against one another.
Milestones across two streams must be compared with age norms before a disposition is chosen. Competitors are narrower investigations that would follow, not precede, the keyed step.
One examination finding names the mechanism directly. Most options are from other response categories and are separable without the decisive finding.
All options are design labels on one taxonomy. Two neighbouring labels stay genuinely live because the scenario omits any comparison group, which is the decisive structural property.
One examination sign is pathognomonic between the two leading competitors, and the stem supplies it explicitly.
Shortest option set in the collection. The mechanism is named by the injury pattern in the stem; the competitors are generic alternatives without stem support.
One competitor is explicitly excluded in the stem, which is a written-in negation rather than a reasoned discriminator. The remaining choice rests on a target-symptom to drug-class mapping.
Sequencing item: several options are correct actions in the wrong order. The decisive point is that physiological instability outranks diagnostic confirmation.
Multiple numeric values must be integrated to a mechanism and then to a step; one competitor is a confirmatory test already made redundant by the data, and another is actively unsafe.
The stem explicitly excludes the highest-salience emergency, which leaves two anatomically adjacent explanations and a management-tier choice between them.

Inverted item form: the candidate must reach an unnamed diagnosis and then predict its auscultatory signature. All options are murmurs, so the response class is tight and no option is separable without the full chain.
A single adverse-effect management principle decides; one competitor is a lifestyle-only measure and one is a non-response option.
Requires naming a withdrawal state and then choosing between substitution, cross-taper and adjunct strategies. All options are dosed regimens, so parallelism is high and no option separates on form.
A time-critical single-agent decision with a canonical answer. Competitors are adjuncts that a candidate may sequence incorrectly but that do not compete for first place.
Options are legal and ethical categories rather than actions. One competitor is a broadly true but non-specific label, which is the main attractor.
A single categorical rule applied to a list; only one option belongs to the excluded class.
A neurological pattern and a pain finding point to different mechanisms; every option is a defensible next step for one of them, so no competitor is separable without weighing both.
Requires interpreting a value against age-referenced norms and then applying a confirm-before-act rule. Competitors are the treatment steps that would follow confirmation.
One reference-standard investigation against structurally unrelated alternatives.
Fever plus focal bony tenderness and refusal to bear weight separate the key from three age-appropriate competitors that share the presenting complaint.

A medication list and a laboratory panel are supplied and each competitor is anchored on exactly one datum. The decisive move is recognising that the most salient candidate datum does not meet its own diagnostic threshold. No competitor is separable on sight.

Prior negative investigations are given to close off the competing pathways, and one functional test result is decisive. Pharmacologic competitors remain live for a candidate who discounts that result.
The decisive link is between a remote surgical history and the anatomical site of bleeding; without making that link the standard bleeding-workup competitors are all defensible.
All options are laboratory tests. One syndrome-specific marker is keyed; two competitors belong to an overlapping but distinct syndrome.
Options mix pharmacologic, psychosocial and behavioural strategies. The decisive point is that the patient is euthymic and adherent, so escalation options are inferior rather than wrong in kind.

The lead-in fixes one prior action and asks for the next, which is a sequencing contract. The most escalatory option is highly attractive and is defeated by a physiological mechanism rather than by an exclusion clause.

A negative confirmatory test reframes the whole presentation. Competitors include escalating the original therapy and two psychosocial actions that differ only in specificity, which is the fine discrimination being tested.

One test's negative predictive value is decisive; every competitor is a correct action for the presentation the test has just made unlikely, so all remain live for a candidate who does not use the result.
A reference table is embedded in the stem to establish that the patient's premise is wrong. The keyed action is an elicitation step and the competitors are assertion, capitulation and dismissal.
Tests whether the candidate resists a patient-initiated request. Competitors are the investigations that would follow if the request were accepted uncritically.
One professional duty decides; two options are refusals and one is an inappropriate prediction of an adjudication outcome.
All options are plausible determinants of intervention success; the key is the one with the strongest evidence base as a predictor, so competitors stay live.
Time since injury and tissue viability jointly decide. Competitors are correct actions for a different injury tier.
Options span a spectrum from false reassurance through vagueness to blame. The key is the accurate, non-blaming factual statement, which is a fine distinction from both neighbours.
The key is phrased as a collaborative elicitation rather than an instruction, which is itself the discrimination. Competitors include a medically true but lower-priority warning.
Two independent findings must be combined into a threshold judgement before the duty is triggered. Competitors are reasonable clinical steps that do not discharge the duty.
Requires arithmetic against two eligibility criteria before choosing a modality. One competitor asserts the eligibility conclusion the arithmetic refutes.
Options mix bereavement care, safety, forensic and administrative actions, so the response class is broader than usual. The key is the bereavement-care action.
Recurrence pattern in a young patient makes a history-taking step the key while every competitor is an escalation to imaging or procedure.
One organ system determines prognosis in the named condition and one option tests it. Competitors have no prognostic role.
One stewardship principle decides. Two competitors are accommodation options and one is a deflection.
A laboratory panel contains three abnormalities that share one upstream cause. Each competitor is anchored on one abnormality treated in isolation, which is the intended error.
A condition-specific first-line agent against generic agents for the presenting sign. Recognition-level for a prepared candidate.
A long laboratory panel with one internally consistent pattern, and a concurrent medication that offers a competing explanation for the same abnormality. Distinguishing the two is the item.

study_bank_difficulty_policy.note: A study-bank design choice, not a measurement and not a reconstruction of any MCC distribution. To be calibrated and superseded once empirical learner-response data exists.
